title: Local roles: ork keeps the anchor log across fresh sessions
lead: *Proposed.* Owner direction 2026-11-16 (relay session 8d711f67, interactive question, "ork keeps anchor log"): ork records what a local role read and searched in each session, from the calls its approval hook already sees, and puts that record in the next session's brief. The model's own progress note stays; ork's record does not depend on it.
findings_note: S304 trial 5 (2026-11-16, run ork-20261116-012801-28aa, S246): the claude-local implementer ran 5 sessions in 90 min with 0 Edits; each session made 16-24 Reads and 11-17 Greps and read internal/daemon/runs.go 7-12 times. Its progress note's anchor log stayed "(none yet)", so the restart brief (`internal/engine/round.go:599-606`) told each new session to trust a note that held nothing, and it re-read the same file.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
*Proposed.* A local model does not keep the note's anchor log while it explores (trials 3 and 5). The approval hook (`internal/agent/claude/pretool.go`, `Evaluate`) sees every Read (path, offset, limit) and Grep (pattern, path) a claude-local role makes, so ork can write the log itself.

Open owner questions (the implementer asks them with `adj ask` first):

- Q1 (`roles.local-read-log-content`): what goes in the record? (a) *recommended*: one line per Read (`path:start-end`) and per Grep (`pattern in path: N hits`), merged so a range read twice shows once, newest last, at most 80 lines. (b) also the first lines of each Grep's hits.
- Q2 (`roles.local-read-log-reuse`): what does the restart brief say about it? (a) *recommended*: "You already read these; do not read them again unless you are about to edit that range." (b) list only, no instruction.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/daemon/approval.go` (append each evaluated Read or Grep of a claude-local role to the run's read log)
- `internal/agent/claude/pretool.go:53` (`Evaluate`: the call's path and range are already parsed)
- `internal/engine/round.go:585-606` (restart brief: the read log under its own heading)
- `internal/daemon/approval_test.go`
- `internal/engine/round_test.go`
- `docs/design.md`
- `docs/state.md` (the read log file in the run dir)
- `CHANGELOG.md`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestApprovalRecordsLocalReads`: three Read calls and one Grep through the approval point leave four entries in the run's read log for that role and round.
- `TestRestartBriefCarriesTheReadLog`: a fresh session's brief holds the merged read log under `## Already read`, after the progress note.
- `TestReadLogMergesRepeatedRanges`: the same `path:1-500` read twice appears once.
- `TestCloudRoleHasNoReadLog`: a cloud role's brief and run dir are unchanged.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. `adj ask` Q1 and Q2 with `--ref` this slice; wait for the owner's answers.
2. Red tests, then the code.
3. Docs: `docs/design.md`, `docs/state.md`. CHANGELOG.md: one bullet under `## Unreleased`.

Owner decisions (2026-11-16): What does ork's read record hold for a Grep, given the hook sees the call but not its result? -> calls only: one line per Read (`path:start-end`) and per Grep (`pattern in path`), with no hit counts. Identical entries merge, newest last, at most 80 lines. Built only from the calls the approval hook already sees. [roles.local-read-log-content]. What does the restart brief say about the read record? -> do not reread: "You already read these; do not read them again unless you are about to edit that range." [roles.local-read-log-reuse].
